docs.title: What is Meowtils?
docs.text: Meowtils is a Minecraft utility mod with features that are focused towards specific servers and gamemodes, as well as general quality of life enhancements that can be useful anywhere.

docs.title: Information
docs.text:
Caution

The only official places to download Meowtils:

  • The official Meowtils website: meowtils.dev

  • The repository: github.com/femboytatp/meowtils

  • My projects website: tatp.wtf

docs.title: Supported Versions
docs.text:
• Forge 1.8.9

  • Lunar Client 1.8.9

Installation Guide

docs.title: Supported Platforms
docs.text:
• Windows

  • Linux

  • Mac

Lunar Injection is supported on all platforms.

In rare cases certain features may only work on Windows, if so that will be disclosed on their respective docs page.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• 70+ Modules For various gamemodes, servers, and just general QOL features.

  • Ingame Stats Like Hypixel stat overlays, but ingame.

  • Clientside Anticheat Detects if players around you use certain cheats.

  • Personal Blacklist Allows you to add players for any reason to your own blacklist, which will then alert you if you meet them ingame.

  • Commands A lot of commands for various things, such as quickly joining a game, checking player stats, or shortcuts for longer commands.

  • Extensions Like a small mod loaded by Meowtils, which lets you add your own features. Could be viewed as a powerful scripting API.

docs.title: Entrypoint
docs.text:
This is your main point of entry, it is called once when your Extension is loaded.

Info

You are required to register modules, classes with events, and so on.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. Create a class called Main.java.

  2. Add a public static method that returns void.

  3. Name it init.

Example

public class Main {

    public static void init() {
        // Register here
    }
}

docs.title: What do you need to register?
docs.text:
Tip

You should init your own stuff here as well.

  • Modules

    Example

    Extension.registerModule(new ExampleModule());

  • Events

    Example

    // Not needed for module classes - that is done automatically
Extension.registerEvent(new ExampleHandler());

  • Commands

    Example

    CommandHandler.register(new ExampleCommand());

  • Slot Background

    Example

    SlotManager.register(new ExampleSlot());

  • Name Icons

    Example

    IconManager.register(new ExampleIcon());

docs.title: Extensions
docs.text:
An Extension is an external file that is loaded by Meowtils, it acts as a bridge that allows you to add features. They could be compared to scripts, except with less limitations.

Modules from extensions will show up in a new category called Extensions.

Danger

Extensions have very few limitations, they have the same permissions as Minecraft does. This means they may execute unwanted or malicious code.

ONLY DOWNLOAD EXTENSIONS FROM TRUSTED SOURCES

Note

These docs make the assumption that you have at least some past experience with java and Minecraft in general.

docs.title: Why use Extensions?
docs.text:
Extensions provide a way to modify Minecraft in many ways without having to load a traditional Forge mod. Additionally they are supported on Lunar Client.

  • Runtime loading.

    Extensions can be loaded during runtime, and swapped whenever. You can update your code while actively playing without ever having to disconnect or restart.

  • No GUI or config code needed.

    This is all handled by Meowtils, you can add modules easily to the existing GUI.

  • No Mod ID.

    Fully hidden from servers, unlike a regular Forge mod.

  • Multi-Client Events.

    Meowtils events are both supported on Lunar Client and Forge, simultaneously. Your features will work on both.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
To use an Extension, simply put it in the extensions folder located in the meowtils folder in your game directory. You can also open this folder ingame by doing /extensions.

Info

Extensions end with .meowtils

docs.title: Loading
docs.text:
Extensions that already exist in your folder are automatically loaded when launching your game.

You can also add, remove, or swap Extensions during runtime and then do /reload to load them.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
Generally you should only register one module per extension, and not combine several unrelated features into one extension.

Tip

It is recommended that you follow standards for clarity and for your own convenience.

docs.title: What is an Extension file?
docs.text: Like a jar, a Meowtils extension is an archive of compiled java class files. This is the same thing a regular Forge mod would be, except with a different file extension (.meowtils not .jar) and content requirements.

docs.title: Decompiling
docs.text:
You can use any java decompiler to decompile an Extension to verify what the code is, and exactly what it is doing.

There are many programs that can be used for decompiling, but also some online websites. This is an example of an online decompiler which doesn't require any downloads at all.

Tip

Some decompilers may only allow files with the .jar file extension, in that case you can temporarily rename it from Extension.meowtils to Extension.jar and it should work. This will not corrupt the file.

docs.title: Extension Limitations
docs.text:
Info

Extensions are seen as additions loaded by Meowtils that provide a bridge between your code and Meowtils. They are treated as scripts with less limitations. They will have certain limitations due to how they are loaded.

docs.title: Mixins
docs.text:
Not Supported

Mixins are not supported.

Since Extensions load at runtime by Meowtils you are unable to use certain things that are required to load before class transformation, while this applies to several things the most notable one is Mixins.

Info

In many cases you won't need Mixins at all, however if you do and are unable to find a way around this limitation, it is recommended that you load your own mod instead.

docs.title: Reflection
docs.text:
Supported

Reflection is supported.

Reflection is a powerful tool that, while not as powerful as Mixins, still provide a way to modify certain things that would have otherwise only been possible through Mixins. For many features that otherwise require Mixins this is a great workaround.

Java Reflection API.

Important

In order to ensure compatibility with both Lunar Client and Forge you will need to include several mappings for fields.

Tip

You can find mappings in the resources directory in Meowtils, you can also use any mapping viewer as long as they include SRG & MCP mappings.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Extensions are very similar to a typical Forge mod, you can easily convert a Forge project to build a Meowtils extension however a simple example project will be provided below.

Note

If you need help, ask HERE.

docs.title: 1: Download project
docs.text: Download the ExampleExtension.

docs.title: 2: Extract the project
docs.text:
Your operating system likely has a tool to extract .zip files already, if not you will have to download one.

7-Zip

docs.title: 3: Open the project
docs.text: IntelliJ IDEA is the recommended program to use. You can follow any Forge modding guide if you want to use something else.

docs.title: 4: Add Meowtils as a library
docs.text:
1. Download Meowtils.

  2. Add the Meowtils.jar to the libs folder at root in your project.

  3. Rename the jar to match what you have defined in the build.gradle, by default this will be meowtils.jar.

Tip

If using IntelliJ IDEA you will be able to view the decompiled Meowtils.jar in your sidebar, this can be used as a reference.

docs.title: Extends
docs.text: import wtf.tatp.meowtils.handler.command.ClientCommand;

docs.title: Overrides
docs.text:
getName()

String, should return your command name.

process(String[] args)

This method is called each time the command is ran, args would be the additional command arguments provided.

getAliases()

Array of command aliases, this lets you assign several aliases to the parent command.

If not overriden it will be left empty.

tabCompleteNames()

Boolean, lets you tab-complete player names in your world if it returns true.

If not overriden it will be false.

docs.title: Registering
docs.text:
You will need to register your commands on init.

Example

 CommandHandler.register(new ExampleCommand());

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
public class ExampleCommand extends ClientCommand {

    @Override
    public String getName() {
        return ("examplecommand");
    }

    @Override
    public void process(String[] args) throws CommandException {
        Meowtils.addMessage("Command ran!");
    }

    // Optional; Don't override if you won't use this
    @Override
    public List<String> getAliases() {
        return Arrays.asList("examplecommand2", "examplecommand3");
    }

    // Optional; Don't override this if you don't need it
    @Override
    public boolean tabCompleteNames() {
        return true;
    }
}

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
These display a small toast notification in bottom-right corner.

// Normal notification, with default text scale
NotificationManager.show(String title, String message, Type type, long time)

// Custom text scale
NotificationManager.show(String title, float titleScale, String message, float messageScale, Type type, long time)

Note

This will not automatically adjust text for you, you will have to make sure your text isn't too long so it goes off-screen, etc.

If setting custom scale; keep it within reasonable scale or else it will also not look correct.

Default title scale: 7

Default message scale: 5

docs.title: Types
docs.text: Determines the type of notification, this only affects what icon is used and the color of the icon + title.

docs.title: Info
docs.text: NotificationManager.Type.INFO

docs.title: Alert
docs.text: NotificationManager.Type.ALERT

docs.title: Warning
docs.text: NotificationManager.Type.WARNING

docs.title: Time
docs.text: The time is in milliseconds and determine how long the notification will be visible for.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: NotificationManager.show("Player Warning", "Player is invisible!", NotificationManager.Type.ALERT, 1500);

docs.title: Prefix
docs.text:
This allows you to change the prefix Meowtils uses for all messages.

Warning

Keep in mind this will conflict with other extensions if they also try to set prefix.

docs.title: Set
docs.text: Prefix.setPrefix(String prefix)

docs.title: Reset
docs.text: Prefix.resetPrefix()

docs.title: Client
docs.text: These messages only appear clientside, for yourself.

docs.title: Message with prefix
docs.text:
Meowtils.addMessage(String message)

Prints a message with the Meowtils prefix.

docs.title: Message without prefix
docs.text:
Meowtils.addCleanMessage(String message)

Prints a message without the Meowtils prefix.

docs.title: Debug message
docs.text:
Meowtils.debugMessage(String message)

Prints a message if debug mode is enabled.

Note

Debug mode is toggled with the /meowdebug command.

docs.title: Server
docs.text: These messages are sent to the server, same as if you were to type a message in chat and send it.

docs.title: Message with prefix
docs.text:
Meowtils.sendMessage(String message)

This sends a message to the server with the prefix Meow ».

Note

This only sends messages to party chat, configured for Hypixel. This means it may not work on all servers and should generally be avoided unless this is your intention.

docs.title: Message without prefix
docs.text:
Meowtils.sendCleanMessage(String message)

Sends specified message to the server.

docs.title: Log messages
docs.text:
These are log messages that will not appear in chat, but in your log.

Tip

You should always log important things, which will help with debugging.

docs.title: Info
docs.text:
Meowtils.info(String msg)

Info

Info log messages should be used for general things, for example to log actions such as what player you fetched stats for.

docs.title: Warn
docs.text:
Meowtils.warn(String msg)

Info

Warn log messages should be used for important things, or potential issues.

docs.title: Error
docs.text:
Meowtils.error(String msg)

Info

Error log messages should be used for things that fail, but aren't potentially game-breaking.

docs.title: Fatal
docs.text:
Meowtils.fatal(String msg)

Info

Fatal log messages should be reserved for game-breaking issues that are fatal to your Extension, or even the whole game.

docs.title: Modifying Values
docs.text:
You can modify @Config values from anywhere, as long as they are public. This includes modules that exist in Meowtils or other loaded extensions.

Warning

You should avoid doing this unless you know what it leads to, as in some cases it may lead to weird bugs or even crashes.

docs.title: Modifying the value
Reading Values
docs.text:
You can read @Config values from anywhere, as long as they are public. This includes modules that exist in Meowtils or other loaded extensions.

Tip

This is useful if you need to check if another feature is enabled, even if it doesn't exist in your extension.

docs.title: Accessing the value
Saving Values
docs.text: This saves a value to the Meowtils config file, commonly used for sub-components but you can save any value if wanted.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. This has to be located in a module class.

  2. Each variable will need the @Config annotation.

  3. You should generally keep it public.

Example

@Config public String mode = "Normal";

docs.title: Save to config
docs.text:
When used in module sub-components, it will automatically be saved to config if updated.

If you are manually setting values you need to save it:

Manual save
ConfigManager.save();

More about setting config values can be found HERE.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Events allow you to hook into various things that happen in Minecraft. These will generally be used to tell your Extension when to run your code.

Meowtils events are very similar to Forge events, however there are a few notable differences which will be explained below alongside some examples.

Warning

In order for your Extension to be compatible with Lunar Client, you must only use Meowtils events. Any Forge events (@SubscribeEvent annotated) will only work on Forge or if you specifically inject Meowtils into "Lunar + Forge".

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: Like Forge, an event method has to be a public method that returns void, the actual method name can be anything but generally you would name it something relevant such as onClientTick.

docs.title: Registering
docs.text:
You will need to register classes that contain events.

Info

You do not need to register module classes to the event bus, as this will be done automatically. This only applies to additional classes where you use events.

Example

Extension.registerEvent(new ExampleHandler());

docs.title: Annotation
docs.text: Like Forge, an event method requires an annotation in order to be discovered. In this case that would be @EventTarget which tells the Meowtils event bus that this is a method that should be called when the relevant event fires.

docs.title: Priority
docs.text:
As shown in the example below you are able to set event priority, same as Forge. It defaults to NORMAL if none are set.

  • HIGHEST

  • HIGH

  • NORMAL

  • LOW

  • LOWEST

Example

@EventTarget(priority = EventPriority.HIGHEST)
public void onClientTick(ClientTickEvent event)...

docs.title: Type
docs.text:
Like Forge your event requires a parameter, the type would be the event you are listening to.

Example

ClientTickEvent

docs.title: Name
docs.text:
The parameter name can be anything and it is just used for your event method to "access" the event.

Example

Normally you would name this "event" or "e".

public void (ClientTickEvent event)...

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Certain events have properties that are important to know about. If an event has specific properties, they would be documented on that specific event page.

docs.title: Phase
docs.text: Event phases determine when events are fired, usually this would have PRE & POST, which means the event either fires before or after Minecraft has ran it's own code for this specific event.

docs.title: Type
docs.text:
Similarly to phases, this determines when a specific event should fire. Usually this would be used for selecting whether or not you should fire your event during world load/unload, or which type of chat message you should listen to.

Tip

In order to prevent your events from firing more than wanted you should always strictly enforce properties. Generally you should only run ClientTickEvent|RenderTickEvent on POST, and ChatReceivedEvent with CHAT.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Events will usually have their own methods, in the example below we will use getPhase() in ClientTickEvent to check the current tick phase.

Info

All events will have available methods documented on its own page.

docs.title: Cancelling
docs.text:
You can cancel some events, which would prevent actions from being performed.

event.setCancelled(true);

Important

You should only cancel events when you know what you are doing and what it would lead to.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
This is an example of a ClientTickEvent that would print a message saying "Hello, player!" in your own chat, every Minecraft tick (20 times a second).

Note

In this case we also check if the local player or world is null, since there is no point in sending a message if there is no chat visible. In some cases this will also prevent crashes, for example if you try to access a player that currently doesn't even exist.

@EventTarget
public void onClientTick(ClientTickEvent event) {
    if (mc.thePlayer == null || mc.theWorld == null || event.getPhase() != ClientTickEvent.Phase.POST) return;
    Meowtils.addMessage("Hello, player!");
}

As you can see, this is very similar to how a typical Forge event would be structured.

docs.title: AttackEntityEvent
docs.text:
This fires each time you attempt to attack any entity.

Cancellable = false

docs.title: Parameter
docs.text: AttackEntityEvent

docs.title: Player
docs.text:
EntityPlayer getPlayer()

Returns EntityPlayer.

docs.title: Target
docs.text:
Entity getTarget()

Returns the target Entity.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
@EventTarget
public void onAttackEntity(AttackEntityEvent event) {
    if (event.getTarget() == null) return;
    Meowtils.addMessage("Attacked: " + event.getTarget());
}

docs.title: ChatReceivedEvent
docs.text:
This fires each time a message appears in your chat.

Cancellable = true

docs.title: Parameter
docs.text: ChatReceivedEvent

docs.title: Type
docs.text:
• CHAT - Normal chat messages.

  • SYSTEM - System messages.

  • ACTION_BAR - Action bar messages (above hotbar).

Tip

In most cases you should only use CHAT, which is what is normally used by default in Forge mods.

docs.title: Component
docs.text:
IChatComponent getComponent()

Returns the IChatComponent of the message.

docs.title: Type
docs.text:
byte getType()

Corresponding to current message type.

Tip

It is recommended to use the type enums shown above instead of a byte.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
@EventTarget
public void onChatReceived(ChatReceivedEvent event) {
    if (event.getType() != ChatReceivedEvent.CHAT) return; // Enforces normal chat messages only
    final String msg = event.getComponent().getUnformattedText();

    if (msg.contains("Meow")) {
        Meowtils.addMessage("Someone said Meow!");
    }
}

docs.title: ClientTickEvent
docs.text:
This fires each client tick, which would normally be 20 times per second.

Cancellable = false

docs.title: Parameter
docs.text: ClientTickEvent

docs.title: Phase
docs.text:
• PRE - Before Minecraft ticks.

  • POST - After Minecraft ticks.

Tip

If you don't know which one to use, use POST. In most cases you will never need to use PRE.

docs.title: Phase
docs.text:
Phase getPhase()

Returns the current tick phase.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
/*
We make sure to return if the player or world doesn't exist, while also enforcing post (end) phase of the tick.
*/
@EventTarget
public void onClientTick(ClientTickEvent event) {
    if (mc.thePlayer == null || mc.theWorld == null) return;
    if (event.getPhase() != ClientTickEvent.Phase.POST) return;
    Meowtils.addMessage("Client tick!");
}

docs.title: EntityJoinWorldEvent
docs.text:
This fires each time an entity joins your world.

Cancellable = false

docs.title: Parameter
docs.text: EntityJoinWorldEvent

docs.title: Entity
docs.text:
Entity getEntity()

Returns the Entity.

docs.title: World
docs.text:
World getWorld()

Returns the World.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
/*
This lists all players that join in chat.
*/
@EventTarget
public void onEntityJoinWorld(EntityJoinWorldEvent event) {
    if (event.getEntity() instanceof EntityPlayer) {
        final EntityPlayer player = (EntityPlayer) event.getEntity();
        if (player == null) return;

        Meowtils.addMessage("Player joined: " + player.getName());
    }
}

docs.title: GuiOpenEvent
docs.text:
This fires each time the player opens a gui.

Cancellable = false

docs.title: Parameter
docs.text: GuiOpenEvent

docs.title: Gui
docs.text:
GuiScreen getGui()

Returns current GuiScreen.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
@EventTarget
public void onGuiOpen(GuiOpenEvent event) {
    if (event.getGui() instanceof GuiChest) {
        Meowtils.addMessage("You opened a chest!");
    }
}

docs.title: KeyInputEvent
docs.text:
This fires each time you press a key.

Cancellable = true

Note

This only applies to keybinds that are set in Minecraft settings.

docs.title: Parameter
docs.text: KeyInputEvent

docs.title: Key
docs.text:
KeyBinding getKey()

Returns the pressed KeyBinding.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
@EventTarget
public void onKeyInput(KeyInputEvent event) {
    if (event.getKey() == mc.gameSettings.keyBindAttack) {
        Meowtils.addMessage("You pressed attack key!");
    }
}

docs.title: MouseInputEvent
docs.text:
This fires each time you press a mouse button.

Cancellable = true

docs.title: Parameter
docs.text: MouseInputEvent

docs.title: Action
docs.text:
• RIGHT_CLICK

  • LEFT_CLICK

  • MIDDLE_CLICK

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Action getAction()

Returns current action as shown above.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
@EventTarget
public void onMouseInput(MouseInputEvent event) {
    if (event.getAction() == MouseInputEvent.Action.MIDDLE_CLICK) {
        Meowtils.addMessage("Prevented you from middle clicking!");
        event.setCancelled(true);
    }
}

docs.title: MovementInputUpdateEvent
docs.text:
This fires before movement input states are updated for your player.

Cancellable = false

docs.title: Parameter
docs.text: MovementInputUpdateEvent

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
@EventTarget
public void onMovementInputUpdate(MovementInputUpdateEvent event) {
    Meowtils.addMessage("Updated movement states.");
}

docs.title: PlayerInteractEvent
docs.text:
This fires each time you interact with a block in the world.

Cancellable = false

docs.title: Parameter
docs.text: PlayerInteractEvent

docs.title: Action
docs.text:
• LEFT_CLICK_BLOCK

  • RIGHT_CLICK_BLOCK

docs.title: Action
docs.text:
Action getAction()

Returns current action as shown above.

docs.title: Player
docs.text:
EntityPlayerSP getPlayer()

Returns EntityPlayerSP.

docs.title: World
docs.text:
WorldClient getWorld()

Returns WorldClient.

docs.title: Block position
docs.text:
BlockPos getPos()

Returns BlockPos.

docs.title: Facing
docs.text:
EnumFacing getFacing()

Returns EnumFacing.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
/*
Sends a message when you right-click a chest.
*/
@EventTarget
public void onPlayerInteract(PlayerInteractEvent event) {
    if (event.getAction() != PlayerInteractEvent.Action.RIGHT_CLICK_BLOCK) return;

    final BlockPos blockPos = event.getPos();
    final TileEntity tileEntity = mc.theWorld.getTileEntity(blockPos);

    if (tileEntity instanceof TileEntityChest) {
        Meowtils.addMessage("Right clicked chest!");
    }
}

docs.title: ReceivePacketEvent
docs.text:
This fires each time your client receives a packet from the server.

Cancellable = true

Warning

Cancelling packets is not safe and can lead to non-vanilla client behaviour that may flag anticheats. Only cancel packets when you know what you are doing.

docs.title: Parameter
docs.text: ReceivePacketEvent

docs.title: Packet
docs.text:
Packet<?> getPacket()

Returns current Packet.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
/*
Prints the content of each chat message packet you receive.
*/
@EventTarget
public void onReceivePacket(ReceivePacketEvent event) {
    if (event.getPacket() instanceof S02PacketChat) {
        final S02PacketChat packet = (S02PacketChat) event.getPacket();
        final String msg = packet.getChatComponent().getUnformattedText();

        if (msg != null) {
            Meowtils.addMessage("You received a chat message: " + msg);
        }
    }
}

docs.title: RenderGameOverlayEvent
docs.text:
This fires each frame.

Cancellable = false

Tip

This should be used for rendering HUD overlays, which would be text in most cases.

docs.title: Parameter
docs.text: RenderGameOverlayEvent

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
@EventTarget
public void onRenderGameOverlay(RenderGameOverlayEvent event) {
    if (mc.thePlayer == null || mc.theWorld == null) return;
    if (mc.currentScreen != null) return;

    Meowtils.drawString("Example HUD text", 10, 10, 1, -1);
}

docs.title: RenderPlayerEvent
docs.text:
This fires for players that are rendered.

Cancellable = false

docs.title: Parameter
docs.text: RenderPlayerEvent

docs.title: Stage
docs.text:
• PRE - Before players render.

  • POST - After players render.

docs.title: Stage
docs.text:
Stage getStage()

Returns the stage as shown above.

docs.title: Partial ticks
docs.text:
float getPartialTicks()

Progress between last and current tick, usually used for interpolation.

docs.title: Renderer
docs.text:
RenderPlayer getRenderer()

Returns RenderPlayer.

docs.title: Player
docs.text:
AbstractClientPlayer getPlayer()

Returns AbstractClientPlayer.

docs.title: X
docs.text:
double getX()

Returns X pos.

docs.title: Y
docs.text:
double getY()

Returns Y pos.

docs.title: Z
docs.text:
double getZ()

Returns Z pos.

docs.title: Yaw
docs.text:
float getYaw()

Returns yaw.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
/*
If a player is invisible this makes them visible again.
*/
@EventTarget
public void onRenderPlayer(RenderPlayerEvent event) {
    if (event.getStage() != RenderPlayerEvent.Stage.PRE) return;
    final EntityPlayer player = event.getPlayer();

    if (player.isInvisible()) {
        player.setInvisible(false);
    }
}

docs.title: RenderStringEvent
docs.text:
This fires when a string is rendered.

Cancellable = false

docs.title: Parameter
docs.text: RenderStringEvent

docs.title: Get
docs.text:
String getString()

Returns the current string.

docs.title: Set
docs.text:
void setString(String string)

Sets the current string.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
/*
This visually replaces your name with "Meow".
*/
@EventTarget(priority = EventPriority.LOWEST)
public void onRenderString(RenderStringEvent event) {
    if (mc.thePlayer == null || mc.theWorld == null || event.getString() == null) return;
    final String playerName = mc.thePlayer.getName();
    final String text = event.getString();

    if (text.contains(mc.thePlayer.getName())) {
        event.setString(text.replace(playerName, "Meow"));
    }
}

docs.title: RenderTickEvent
docs.text:
This fires each render tick, which is once per frame.

Cancellable = false

Note

You should always use RenderGameOverlayEvent or RenderWorldLastEvent for render modules. It is recommended that you only use this event when you need to update something faster than what is possible with client tick.

docs.title: Parameter
docs.text: RenderTickEvent

docs.title: Phase
docs.text:
• PRE - Before Minecraft render tick.

  • POST - After Minecraft render tick.

Tip

If you don't know which one to use, use POST. In most cases you will never need to use PRE.

docs.text:
/*
We make sure to return if the player or world doesn't exist, while also enforcing post (end) phase of the render tick.
*/
@EventTarget
public void onRenderTick(RenderTickEvent event) {
    if (mc.thePlayer == null || mc.theWorld == null) return;
    if (event.getPhase() != RenderTickEvent.Phase.POST) return;
    Meowtils.addMessage("Render tick!");

/*
This draws a 3D ESP box on your own player.
*/
@EventTarget
public void onRenderWorldLast(RenderWorldLastEvent event) {
    if (mc.thePlayer == null || mc.theWorld == null) return;

    for (EntityPlayer player : mc.theWorld.playerEntities) {
        if (player == null) continue;
        if (player != mc.thePlayer) continue; // Skip other players

        final Color color = ColorUtil.getColor(255, 255, 255); // White color

        Render.drawEntityBox(player, true, false, color, true, color, 0.1f, 0.1f, 0.1f);
    }
}

/*

You need to register this the same way components are registered.

docs.title: Module Setup
docs.text:
Modules will show up in a new category called Extensions, they will behave like any other module in Meowtils. You will also be able to add components to a module if you want to add settings.

Tip

You should generally make one Extension per module, to keep features separate. This is seen as the standard, however it is up to you as adding several modules to an Extension is still possible.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. Must extend wtf.tatp.meowtils.extension.Extension

  2. Contain @Config public boolean enabled = false;

    This is used for your module state. In this case we set it to false by default, which is the standard.

  3. Contain @Config public int key = 0;

    This is used for your module toggle bind. In this case we set it to 0 by default, which means no key is bound to it.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
public class ExampleModule extends Extension {

    @Config public boolean enabled = false;
    @Config public int key = 0;

    public ExampleModule() {
        super("ExampleModule", "Meowtils"); // Module name & author (you)
        // Register components & tooltip here!
    }
}

docs.text:
int y = 10;
for (String line : lines) {
    Meowtils.drawString(line, 10, y, 1, -1);
    y += Meowtils.offsetString(1);
}

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Tip

You should check Minecraft.getMinecraft().currentScreen to limit drawing your text so it only shows up when you want it to, like in the example below which will only draw the text when no GUI is open.

@EventTarget
public void onRenderGameOverlay(RenderGameOverlayEvent event) {
    if (mc.theWorld == null) return;
    if (mc.currentScreen != null) return;

    final String[] lines = {
            "Meow!",
            "Meow2!",
            "Meow3!"
    };

    int y = 10;

    for (String line : lines) {
        Meowtils.drawString(line, 10, y, 1, -1);
        y += Meowtils.offsetString(1);
    }
}

docs.title: Render Name Icons
docs.text:
This lets you add icons or text to player nametags, which will show up in both tablist & nametags depending on how you limit it.

Bug

If you are using Lunar Client nametag icons will only be displayed in tablist.

docs.title: Interface
docs.text: import wtf.tatp.meowtils.manager.icons.IconProvider;

docs.title: Overrides
docs.text:
Info

You can skip overriding these if you have no intentions of modifying the prefix/suffix. Additionally, tablist or nametag booleans will only return true if they are for the tablist/nametag. Check the example below.

getPrefix(GameProfile profile, boolean tablist, boolean nametag)

String, used for setting prefix (what comes before) the player name.

getSuffix(GameProfile profile, boolean tablist, boolean nametag)

String, used for setting suffix (what comes after) the player name.

docs.title: Registering
docs.text:
You will need to register your implementation at init.

Example

IconManager.register(new ExampleIcon());

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
/*
This displays a prefix and suffix for yourself that says if it is currently being rendered in tablist or nametag.
*/
public class ExampleIcon implements IconProvider {

    @Override
    public String getPrefix(GameProfile profile, boolean tablist, boolean nametag) {
        if (profile.getId() != Minecraft.getMinecraft().thePlayer.getUniqueID()) return "";
        if (tablist) {
            return "Tablist ";
        }
        return "Nametag ";
    }

    @Override
    public String getSuffix(GameProfile profile, boolean tablist, boolean nametag) {
        if (profile.getId() != Minecraft.getMinecraft().thePlayer.getUniqueID()) return "";
        if (tablist) {
            return " Tablist";
        }
        return " Nametag";
    }
}

/*

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text: This guide will briefly go over on how to use Meowtils ingame.

docs.title: GUI Bind
docs.text:
By default the bind for opening the GUI is right shift. However this can be changed in the GUI Module.

Note

If you are unable to open the GUI this way, you can either use the /bind command to bind it to another key, or by using the /meowtilsgui command to open the GUI for you.

docs.title: Navigating the GUI
docs.text: There are several different categories that contain modules, the main category is called Meowtils and this is where you would find general mod settings, rather than actual modules. These are always shown as enabled.

docs.title: Opening a category
docs.text: In order to open or close a category, you can right-click while hovering over it. You can also drag these categories around to organize your GUI.

docs.title: Enabling a module
docs.text: Hover over a module and left-click in order to toggle it.

docs.title: Showing module settings
docs.text:
If you hover over a module and right-click it, the module will expand to show its settings. If a module does not have any settings it will not expand.

To interact with a setting itself, hover over it and left-click.

docs.title: Binding a module
docs.text: You are able to bind modules to a specified key, if so they will toggle when pressing that key. To bind a module middle-click your mouse while hovering over it. Now you are able to assign a key, and you can hit backspace to clear it.

docs.title: Scrolling
docs.text: In case a category is too long you can hover over it and use your scroll wheel to access settings or modules that are located lower down.

docs.title: HUD Editor
docs.text:
The HUD Editor allows you to change the position of HUD Elements from modules. To open it, you can find a button in the bottom left corner while the GUI is opened, if you click it then the HUD Editor will open.

It will display a preview for elements, you can hover over them to see a description of what module it comes from, and you can drag & drop them anywhere.

Info

Only HUD Elements in currently enabled modules will have a preview displayed.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
You may view a list of all commands by doing /meow.

Tip

If a command overrides a server command, you can use /send <command> to send it directly to the server, skipping client commands entirely.

docs.title: External files
docs.text:
All files that Meowtils create, such as config file or lists will be located in your game directory, in its own Meowtils folder. You normally don't have to interact with these unless you want to add custom skins or capes.

Tip

You can open the Meowtils folder in-game by doing /meowfolder.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Info

Meowtils is a one-time installation, after following these steps it will always inject into your game at startup.

Any future updates will be handled by the Auto-Updater, which means you won't have to manually replace any files or install it again.

The Auto-Updater can still be disabled if you want to update manually.

docs.title: 1: Install Forge
docs.text:
If you already have Forge installed you can skip this step.

Warning

You can use third-party launchers for Forge, such as Prism Launcher or Feather Client, however these will have different installation steps.

Certain launchers may not be supported.

  1. Download Forge Installer.

  2. Execute the installer by clicking/opening it.

  3. In the window, select Install client, then click OK.

  4. After installation is complete, open your Minecraft Launcher and select Forge in your versions dropdown menu (where you select which Minecraft version to use). This menu is found when making/editing installations. Full name: release 1.8.9-forge1.8.9-11.15.1.2318-1.8.9

  5. Launch your game once to create the necessary files, or manually navigate to your instance folder (by default, .minecraft), then create a folder called mods.

Note

If you are unable to run the .jar, you will need to install Java.

docs.title: 2: Add Meowtils
docs.text:
1. Download Meowtils.

  2. Add the Meowtils jar to your mods folder.

docs.title: 3: Launch Minecraft
docs.text:
Now launch Minecraft, Meowtils should be loaded.

It is recommended that you check out Basic Usage in order to learn how to use Meowtils.

docs.title: Server Safety
docs.text:
Info

Meowtils is NOT a cheat client, that is past our scope and we have no intentions of being associated as such.

Unlike other mods we do not forcefully restrict our features, even if they may be disallowed. Whatever you want to use is completely up to you, however all features that could be disallowed are already disabled by default.

While modules are specifically made to not cause any detection issues regardless by simulating vanilla game behaviour, certain modules do perform actions for you that, if used on strict anticheats, may end up causing issues. An example of this would be AutoChest with a low delay or certain DelayRemover options.

Warning

You are in complete control of what modules and settings you use, as well as which servers you play on. This is use at your own risk.

We are not responsible for your mistakes.

docs.title: Restricting Features
docs.text:
You are able to restrict modules to comply with server rules, this can be changed in the GUI Module.

Restricting modules is done by you, and can be changed by you at any time. While modules are restricted they will be disabled and hidden from the GUI.

Every module has a Risk Label that determines how safe it is.

docs.title: Risk Labels
docs.text:
Legit

Legit modules are not considered to be unfair as they provide no real advantage, or because similar features already exist in popular legit modifications such as Lunar Client, they are considered no-risk modules.

Safe

While not guaranteed, safe modules may provide an unfair advantage, but they are client-side only which means they are considered low-risk modules as it is not possible to detect them.

Blatant

Blatant modules provide a significant advantage, and may be detected by anticheats due to how they behave. These would be considered high-risk modules.

docs.title: Default Features
docs.text: These features are always enabled, but they do not provide any unfair advantages.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
There are many different commands, you may view all by doing /meow.

Info

Commands do not provide an unfair advantage.

docs.title: Resource Exploit Fix
docs.text:
This prevents servers from looking through your directories to find files that may indicate you are cheating, or to attempt fingerprinting you.

Info

This is considered a security exploit and is already fixed by most modifications, such as the Patcher Mod and Lunar Client.

docs.text:
Uses the Hypixel API to fetch stats.

Hypixel API

In order to use the Hypixel API you need a key.

How to obtain an API key:

  1. Go to Hypixel Developer Dashboard.

  2. Sign in with your Hypixel forums account.

  3. Click CREATE API KEY

  4. In-game, add your key with /meowapi <key>

Normal keys don't last forever and will have to be regenerated. You may also need a forums account that is older than a day.

Uses the Abyss Overlay API for fetching stats, does not require any API key.

Warning

We simply provide the alternative for you to use this, but they likely do not intend for their API to be used this way, and if abused they might ban you.

As long as it is used normally (loading stats ingame) you shouldn't run into any issues as this is what their overlay already does.

docs.text:
1. Open filter folder, can be done with /meowfilter folder in-game.

  2. Add your filter.

  3. Type the filter name in the module text box, or use /meowfilter select <name> command.

  4. Reload, either with the button in the module or with /meowfilter reload.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
In order for ChatFilter to know which messages should be filtered, you need to use the operators shown below.

The operators need to be in front of the text you want to filter, with no spaces.

You can also put ! in front of an operator, if so it is reversed. As an example EQUALS becomes DOES NOT EQUAL. These will all be documented below.

Info

Filters should be .txt files. Each line is handled separately, and text is case-insensitive.

Tip

You can use the default.txt filter as a reference.

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
#: Comment

Any text after a comment will be ignored, a comment has to be at the start of a line. You can use comments to temporarily disable filter rules without having to delete them, or to document anything that is necessary, which is good practise if you plan to share your filter.

Example

# This is a comment

docs.title: Allowed server

If you want it to work everywhere, you can leave this out or put it as -all.

-hypixel

It is recommended that you keep these enabled, or that you manually update each new version that is available. Outdated versions may contain fatal bugs, instability issues, performance issues, and outdated features.

docs.title: How do they work?
docs.text: Each time you join a world for the first time the update checker will run, this contacts the GitHub API to check the latest version available from the Meowtils Repo.

docs.title: When enabled:
docs.text:
If your current version is older, it will download the new jar. When you close your game the old jar will get replaced by the new one, to apply the new update next time you launch.

This also downloads the MeowtilsAutoUpdate.jar, which is what applies the update after your game closes. This will only be downloaded if you are missing it, not each update.

docs.title: When disabled:
docs.text:
This will just alert you in chat if you use an outdated version, and provide a link if you want to go download it manually.

Note

This requires you to properly replace the jar, which if using Lunar Client also requires you to rename it.

docs.title: Blacklist
docs.text:
The blacklist allows you to add players for any reason to a list that keeps track of them. This is your own personal blacklist and is stored in your game directory with other mod files.

It stores their name, timestamp of when they were blacklisted, and then what reasons they are blacklisted for.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Blacklisting a player:

/blacklist | /bl <player> <reasons> - Add to blacklist.

The reasons should be separated by a space, with the exception of "legit scaffold" which will be treated as one reason. If no reason is provided while blacklisting it will fall back to "cheating" as a generic reason.

/unblacklist | /ubl <player\> - Remove from blacklist.

/blacklist info | /bl info <player\> - Shows blacklist info.

Example

/bl tatp autoblock killaura fakelag

docs.title: Icons
docs.text:
Blacklisted players will have an icon in tablist and their nametag, depending on how you configure the Icons Module.

The blacklist icon color depends on what reasons they are blacklisted for, this is based on priority which means the color will represent the highest severity reason they are blacklisted for.

⚠ = Highest severity blatant cheat reason

⚠ = Medium severity closet cheat reason

⚠ = Blacklisted & safelisted at the same time

⚠ = Any other custom reason

docs.title: Alerts
docs.text:
You can enable alerts so if a player that is blacklisted shows up in your world, it will send you a warning.

This can be enabled in the Notifications Module.

docs.title: Reasons
docs.text:
These are the pre-defined reasons provided, and their color will follow the severity as shown above. If you are blacklisting for a reason that is not pre-defined it will instead show up as green.

Note

This requires you to register a GitHub account, alternatively you can join Mega's Discord Server for support.

docs.title: Try this before reporting a bug:
docs.text:
• Remove all your mods except for Meowtils.

    Mod Conflicts

    In some cases issues appear due to a mod conflict, if so you should still report this as a bug so we can investigate, as we can sometimes fix this conflict on our end.

    Make sure to specify that its due to a conflict and what mod was causing it in your bug report.

  • Temporarily remove all Extensions.

    Extensions

    Extensions can cause issues or crashes, you should remove them to make sure they are not the reason. If an extension is at fault, you should contact the author of that extension instead.

  • Verify Hypixel language is set to English.

    Language

    Many features depend on scoreboard or chat text, make sure your Hypixel language is set to English.

  • Try a new instance of Minecraft.

    New Instance

    Sometimes a fresh instance can solve issues with launching.

    How to create a fresh instance:

    1. Create a new folder called .minecraft2

    2. In your launcher, add .minecraft2 as the path instead of the default .minecraft

    3. Launch your game once to download any necessary files

    4. Now launch with your mods, including Meowtils

  • Use the official Minecraft launcher.

    Different Launcher

    While most launchers that support Forge should generally work, some may not. Alternatively you could try using a different launcher from the one you are currently experiencing an issue with.

  • Reinstall Java.

    Java

    If you have issues with crashing try to re-install java.

    Steps:

    1. Uninstall java.

    2. Restart computer (optional but recommended).

    3. Reinstall java.

    4. Restart computer again (optional but recommended).

    5. Attempt to launch again.

docs.title: File Safety
docs.text:
Info

The only official places to download Meowtils is: - meowtils.dev - github.com/femboytatp/meowtils - tatp.wtf

Like everything else, you should always be careful when running unknown files. In certain cases they may perform malicious actions. The file type Meowtils is shipped as (.jar, also known as a java archive) can be malicious, especially when you launch it as a mod which will automatically grant it the same permissions as Minecraft does itself, which is a LOT. This is why it is very important you should only ever download it from a trusted source.

docs.title: Obfuscation
docs.text: Many mods & clients are obfuscated, while this is usually a protective measure for auth & protecting their own code from being re-used/copied, it also means the real functionality of the code is being hidden and it may perform harmful actions - without your knowledge. This is not a warning sign in itself, especially if the service you use is paid, however it is something to note and you should never run anything you don't trust completely.

docs.title: Meowtils
docs.text: Meowtils code itself is not obfuscated in any way, however it is compiled with vanilla obfuscation (also known as "notch" obfuscation), applying to classes & fields & method names. All of these can be remapped manually by you, the Meowtils.jar even contains a '.csv' file with all of the mappings.

docs.title: Meowtils Injectable
docs.text: We provide an .exe file for full runtime-injection. Internally this does nothing different from the regular Meowtils.jar other than a few smaller launch differences, mainly attaching to the JVM at runtime and transforming classes again. Due to how it behaves, it might be flagged by anti-virus programs.

docs.title: Windows Defender
docs.text:
1. Open Windows Security

  2. Go to Virus & threat protection

  3. Click Manage settings under "Virus & threat protection settings"

  4. Scroll down and click Add or remove exclusions

  5. Click Add an exclusion > File

  6. Navigate to your Downloads folder and select the Meowtils exe.
